thread:
alex: Hello — need to add my spouse to health and dental. We were married in Brazil in 2023 but the local certificate needs an apostille and English translation. Spouse arrived on a dependent visa 2024-01-10. Can we get coverage starting 2024-01-10? SSN not issued yet.

rafael (Benefits): Hi Alex — welcome! Short answer: probably yes, but we need specific docs. For foreign marriage + retro effective date we require: marriage cert (original scan), apostille or consular legalization, certified English translation, spouse passport + visa/I-94, proof of cohabitation or joint bank if available, and SSN receipt or ITIN application if SSN pending.

alex: Got it. Apostille is in progress with the consulate — should take ~2 weeks. I have the untranslated cert and passport scans now. If I submit now with a note that apostille is pending, will you accept provisional enrollment?

rafael (Benefits): We can open a provisional case but carriers usually require final paperwork before fully backdating. Upload what you have to Workday > Benefits > Add Dependent and put subject: ADD SPOUSE: Alex Lastname / Spouse Lastname - BRAZIL MARRIAGE - EFFECTIVE 2024-01-10 - PROVISIONAL. Include whatever docs you have and the expected apostille date.

tasha (People Ops): Also include a short affidavit from you confirming marriage date and spouse arrival date; that speeds review. If apostille arrives after docs window (30 days QLE), we may still accept but Legal might need to confirm. CC me on the upload.

payroll (Payroll): FYI on proration — if we set effective 2024-01-10 and payroll cycles have closed for January, premiums will be recouped over the next 2 pay runs. Send us the spouse's hire/add date in the Workday form so we calculate accurately. We'll use alternate ID if SSN missing; attach proof of SSN application if available to avoid duplicate record creation when SSN arrives.

legal-bot (Legal): Reminder: for foreign civil documents, carrier acceptance may depend on apostille vs consular legalization. If you used a certified translation from a sworn translator, include translator declaration. If apostille not issued, include consular attestation steps taken.

rafael (Benefits): Quick checklist to paste into upload body:
- marriage_certificate_scan.pdf (original language)
- apostille_receipt_or_apostille.pdf OR consular_attestation.pdf
- marriage_translation_certified.pdf (certified English translation + translator declaration)
- passport_spouse.pdf (ID page + visa page)
- i94_or_arrival_receipt.pdf
- affidavit_signed_self.pdf (1 page)
- ssn_receipt_or_itin_application.pdf (if available)
- proof_of_address_or_joint_account.pdf (optional)
Case ID: PO-2024-3620

alex: Thanks. If the spouse needs the medical visit on 2024-01-18 should I file a retrospective claim now or wait until full docs are in?

rafael (Benefits): Upload the claim receipt now and flag it: URGENT RETRO CLAIM. We'll include it with the retro packet but note carriers can deny retrospective claims if final docs are missing. Still worth submitting.

tasha (People Ops): One more thing: HSA/FSA midyear changes — if you add spouse, your FSA/HSA eligibility could change. Want me to loop Benefits Ops to advise on pre-tax contributions?

alex: Yes please on HSA impact. I'm on HSA family plan? currently single coverage.

rafael (Benefits): If you switch from single to family HSA midyear we can prorate contribution limits and FSA elections. We'll send a summary once enrollment is processed.

hrbot (People Ops Bot): Case created PO-2024-3620. Link: https://internal.redwood/cases/PO-2024-3620 (internal). Please include case ID in Workday upload subject line.

alex: Uploaded marriage cert, passport, and affidavit to Workday and noted apostille ETA 2024-02-05. CC'd tasha.

rafael (Benefits): Received. I'll validate docs and mark provisional. If apostille arrives within 14 days we expect carrier backdate approval to 2024-01-10. If not, we'll escalate to Legal.

payroll (Payroll): Noted for deductions. We'll prepare proration schedule and send once Benefits confirms effective date.

alex: Appreciate it — fingers crossed :slightly_smiling_face:
